title: Today and the daily checklist
body: Today shows your progress for the current day of Ramadan, your next prayer or iftar time, the hadith of the day and the checklist of deeds in seven groups: salah and dhikr, Quran, character, charity, the last ten nights (from day 21), things to avoid, and the Abu Bakr challenge. Tick a deed when you have done it. Turn on detail mode to see each deed's source, a short explanation and its authenticity grade.

title: Points and progress
body: Each deed is worth a few points, shown next to it. Your daily percentage is the share of today's deeds you ticked. Points earned on days 21 to 30 count one and a half times, because the Prophet ﷺ strove hardest in the last ten nights (Muslim 1175).

title: Quran tracker
body: Log the pages you read after each session. The standard Madani mushaf has 604 pages in 30 juz, so about 20 pages a day completes it in Ramadan. The tracker shows your juz, the pace you need for the days left, and a chart of your reading.

title: Learn: quiz and flashcards
body: Learn turns the hadith and verses behind every deed into true-or-false cards, multiple-choice questions and flashcard decks (Ramadan words, duas, verses about fasting, Sunnahs of fasting, Ramadan in history, Quran facts and preparing for Ramadan). Flashcards use spaced repetition: cards you know come back less often, cards you miss come back sooner. Today's 5 is a short daily mix that builds a learning streak. Every answer shows its source.

title: Ramadan Prep
body: A 30-day programme to get ready before Ramadan begins. It starts with a short self-check, then gives three small actions each day: first fixing your salah (praying on time, Fajr, the Sunnah prayers, understanding what you recite), then building a daily connection with the Quran, then fasting practice and habits, and finally the heart, family and charity. Daily salah and Quran check-ins show your readiness. During Sha'ban the plan follows the Hijri date, so it ends as Ramadan begins; you can also start it at any time from the Me tab.

title: Competitions
body: Schools, universities, mosques, companies, families and communities can run a Ramadan competition. An organiser creates one with up to ten prizes and shares the six-letter join code, a QR poster or personal invitation links. Participants join with the code and a display name; their points, days logged and Quran pages update a live leaderboard for individuals and for classes or teams. Only a display name and totals are shared, never which deeds you ticked. Organisers can set a daily points cap, review flagged entries, export results and print certificates for everyone at Eid.

title: Prayer times and iftar
body: Allow your location (or enter coordinates) to see today's prayer times and a countdown to iftar and to the end of suhoor. Choose the calculation method your community follows in settings. Your location stays on your device unless you turn on reminders.

title: Streaks
body: Four streaks count consecutive days on which you ticked Fajr, Isha, any Quran deed (recitation, reflection or listening) and charity (giving charity or feeding a fasting person). The Prophet ﷺ said the most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small (Bukhari 6464).

title: The 12 badges
body: First Step: tick anything on day 1. Week One: log something on each of days 1 to 7. Halfway: log something on each of days 1 to 15. Fajr Warrior: a 7-day Fajr streak. Tahajjud Master: Tahajjud on 7 nights. Quran Lover: recitation or reflection on 15 days. Generous: charity on 10 days. Abu Bakr: all four Abu Bakr deeds in one day. Abu Bakr Gold: that on 3 different days. Last 10 Hero: at least 5 of the last ten days logged with an average of 70% or more. Perfectionist: 100% on 3 days. Champion: 60% or more on 20 days.

title: The last ten nights
body: In the Islamic calendar each night comes before its day, so the 21st night begins at sunset on day 20. From that evening the app marks the odd nights (21, 23, 25, 27 and 29) on the evenings they begin, and from day 21 the checklist adds a section for the last ten days and nights. The Prophet ﷺ told us to seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten (Bukhari 2017), so make the most of each of them.

title: Sisters' mode
body: Turn this on during your period. Prayer and fasting deeds are set aside and left out of your percentage, so your score reflects the worship that applies to you: dhikr, dua, listening to the Quran, charity, service and character.

title: Modes and the Hijri date
body: The app follows the Hijri calendar (Umm al-Qura). In Ramadan it sets the day automatically, in Sha'ban it suggests Ramadan Prep, and the rest of the year it tracks Sunnah fasts (Mondays, Thursdays and the 13th to 15th of each month), the six days of Shawwal and the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah. If your community sighted the moon a day earlier or later, adjust it by one day in settings. You can also choose the mode yourself.

title: Reflection journal and Eid report
body: Write a line each day about what you learned or want to improve. On Eid, download a PDF report with your days, Quran pages, streaks, badges and reflections — a keepsake, and a way to celebrate children's effort.

title: Account and sync
body: Everything works without an account and stays on your device. Create one if you want a backup and to sync between phone, tablet and computer. You can delete the account and its cloud data at any time.

title: Languages
body: The app is available in English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Bengali, Portuguese, Russian and Urdu, with right-to-left layout for Arabic and Urdu. Translations of hadith and verse meanings are for understanding; follow the source link for the authoritative text.

title: Privacy and your data
body: Your tracker data lives on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you join a competition (display name and totals), create an account (for sync), turn on reminders, share your progress, or use the explain feature. Export a backup file or reset everything from the data section.
